Abstract & Project Motivation

Modern consumers actively purchase apparel but consistently underutilize over 70% of their wardrobe. This stems from visual closet disorganization, styling friction, and the tedious requirement of existing apps that force users to type metadata for clothes one by one. FitChecker is an autonomous, privacy-preserving digital wardrobe and stylist engineered to solve these bottlenecks.

FitChecker introduces an end-to-end computer vision and machine learning pipeline that automatically cuts out garments from smartphone photos onto pure studio white (#FFFFFF), infers garment category, fit, pattern, and formality without manual tagging, provides high-fashion editorial styling rules, and formulates daily outfit combinations through a multi-objective mathematical scoring rubric.

FUNCTION 1: SMART DIGITAL WARDROBE GALLERY

The Digital Wardrobe Gallery provides an interactive visual inventory of a user's entire apparel collection. It groups garments by intuitive categories (Tops, Bottoms, Footwear, Layers, One-Piece), displays formality ratings (Casual 1 to Black Tie 5), wear counters, and dominant color swatches.

Key Capabilities

  • Categorical Partitioning: Instant filtering by tops, bottoms, outerwear, and footwear.
  • Wear Frequency Tracking: Records wear count and last-worn timestamp to prevent repetitive outfits.
  • Formality Badges: Formality level displayed as a clean visual indicator (1-5).
  • Color Palette Dots: Real-time rendering of extracted fabric hex codes.
Figure 1.1: Multi-User Profile Selector & Wardrobe Partitioning

FUNCTION 2: AI BACKGROUND ISOLATION & STUDIO CLEANER

Photographing garments in everyday rooms introduces messy backgrounds: bedroom walls, bedsheets, hangers, and carpets. FitChecker features an autonomous background isolation engine powered by OpenCV GrabCut with Adaptive Perimeter Sampling.

Technical Breakthrough: Standard segmentation fails when garments touch boundaries or when room walls are textured. FitChecker uses adaptive perimeter sampling rect = (bx, by, W - 2*bx, H - 2*by) with cv2.GC_INIT_WITH_RECT, paired with blue hanger clearance in HSV color space and cavity-preserving connected component analysis.

→
FITCHECKER CUTOUT (Solid #FFFFFF)

FUNCTION 3 & 4: AI GARMENT IDENTIFICATION & EDITORIAL STYLING ENGINE

When a garment photo is ingested, FitChecker's computer vision engine instantly analyzes its structural silhouette and fabrics. It displays two complementary intelligent cards: AI Garment Identification and AI Editorial Styling Advice.

Figure 3.1: Live Application Screenshot — AI Garment Identification and AI Editorial Styling Advice with Color Match Percentages and Proportion Rules

Function 3: AI Garment Identification

Extracts spatial geometry directly from the foreground mask:

  • Aspect Ratio (H/W): Separates footwear (AR < 0.65), standard tops, and elongated bottoms/kurtas (AR > 1.45).
  • Placket Edge Density: Vertical Canny edge filters down the chest line identify button plackets, preventing collared shirts from being mistaken for blazers.
  • Leg Bifurcation: Horizontal density scan at 70% height detects leg splits in trousers and shorts.
  • Formality Ingress: Dark navy, charcoal, and structured lapels automatically score formality 4/5 or 5/5.

Function 4: AI Editorial Styling Advice

Replaces generic fashion cliches with editorial rules:

  • Ideal Color Pairings: Curated compatibility percentages (e.g., Beige 82%, Black 82%, Blue 82%).
  • Recommended Layering: Direct garment layering suggestions (e.g., Crewneck T-Shirt as Layer 1, Tailored Trousers as Bottom).
  • Footwear Anchor: Exact footwear styles to balance the silhouette (Dress Shoes, Loafers, Minimalist Sneakers).
  • Proportion Rules: Explains visual volume balance (e.g. structured upper volume paired with clean tapered lower silhouette).

FUNCTION 5: MULTI-CRITERIA DAILY OUTFIT RECOMMENDER

The outfit engine evaluates combinations of tops, bottoms, layers, and footwear from the user's wardrobe. It uses a mathematically explainable Multi-Objective Weighted Scoring Function:

Outfit Score = 0.30 × Occasion + 0.25 × Color + 0.20 × StyleFormality + 0.15 × Weather + 0.10 × Preference − RecencyPenalty

Mathematical Breakdown of Scoring Components

Scoring Component Weight Underlying Mathematical Metric
Occasion Suitability 30% 100 - 20 × |Formality_garment - Formality_target| + 15 × StyleTagMatch
Color Harmony 25% Pairwise color matrix + HSV difference (|ΔH - 180°| < 20° for complementary)
Style & Formality Match 20% Variance penalty across ensemble: max(0, 100 - 25 × FormalityVariance)
Weather Suitability 15% Season & fabric weight compatibility with current temperature context
Personal Preference 10% Historical wear counts and user feedback thumbs-up ratings
Recency Decay Penalty Deduction −25 points if worn within 3 days; −15 points if worn within 7 days

FUNCTION 6: PERSONAL COLORIMETRY & 24 FOUNDATION SHADES

Traditional four-season systems ("Cool Summer", "Warm Autumn") confuse consumers with subjective cosmetology terms. FitChecker maps complexion to 24 clinical foundation shades grouped across 6 intuitive tiers:

Figure 6.1: Personal Color & Complexion Guidance Page with Direct Palette Recommendations

Complexion Tiers & Vitiligo Innovation

Fair Porcelain (Cool), Light Warm Peach (Warm), Medium Olive, Medium Golden, Rich Dusky, and Deep Espresso: Each tier receives curated "Best Colors", "Warmth Boosters", and "Colors to Avoid".

Specialized Vitiligo Duo-Tone Mode: For users with vitiligo, single-palette algorithms wash out one tone or clash with another. FitChecker formulates dual-palette recommendations harmonizing deep base skin with lighter pigmentation patches.

FUNCTION 7: BATCH UPLOAD STUDIO (UP TO 20 CLOTHES AT ONCE)

Uploading wardrobe items one by one is the #1 reason users abandon digital closet apps. FitChecker features a high-throughput Batch Upload Studio allowing users to ingest up to 20 garment photos simultaneously.

Figure 7.1: Add Clothing Page with Color Extraction and Background Removal

Batch Engine Workflow

  1. Multi-File Ingestion: Drag and drop 2 to 20 photos at once.
  2. Session-State Caching: All cutouts and dominant colors are processed once and cached in st.session_state["batch_cache"].
  3. Editable Grid Review: A responsive card grid displays thumbnails, category dropdowns, fit, and pattern selectors.
  4. Atomic Bulk Save: Single-click commit writes all garments to wardrobe.csv and saves transparent PNG cutouts atomically.

FUNCTION 8: MULTI-USER DATA ISOLATION & MASTER SECURITY PIN

To enable sharing the application with friends and family without mixing up wardrobes or compromising personal data, FitChecker implements Namespace Directory Partitioning.

Directory-Level Data Isolation

Each user profile operates inside an isolated sandbox directory:

user_data/users/<username>/
  └ wardrobe.csv
  └ outfits.csv
  └ feedback.csv
  └ images/

Switching profiles completely resets memory references and points all database queries strictly to the active user's folder.

Master Creator Security PIN (7777)

The Master Creator account is protected with PIN verification:

  • Friends can create their own profiles and manage private wardrobes.
  • Switching to the Creator profile requires entering the secret 4-digit PIN (7777).
  • Prevents accidental overwrites, snooping, or wardrobe contamination.

THE AI & MACHINE LEARNING TOOLS USED TO BUILD FITCHECKER

FitChecker was engineered through a synergy of modern artificial intelligence, computer vision libraries, and agentic software design tools:

1. Google Antigravity & DeepMind Agentic Pair Programming

The entire software architecture, mathematical scoring formulas, and computer vision routines were designed and refined using Google Antigravity — DeepMind's state-of-the-art agentic AI development environment.

  • Autonomous Iterative Debugging: The AI agent diagnosed complex computer vision artifacts (such as underarm cavity fillings and placket edge frequencies) in real time.
  • Continuous Automated Test Harness: Formulated and maintained a rigorous 130-test regression suite ensuring zero breaking changes across updates.
  • Subagent Task Delegation: Utilized specialized subagents to perform sandbox testing and mathematical rubric validation concurrently.

2. OpenCV (Open Source Computer Vision)

  • Iterative GrabCut Segmentation: Uses dual 5-component Gaussian Mixture Models to perform min-cut energy optimization on pixel contrast boundaries.
  • Canny Edge Detection: High-frequency edge filters isolating vertical shirt plackets and lapel contours.
  • Laplacian Texture Variance: Measures second-order spatial derivatives to detect Plain, Checked, and Striped fabric textures.

3. Scikit-Learn Machine Learning Ensemble

  • Random Forest Classifier: 100-tree ensemble learning user acceptance probabilities from feedback logs.
  • Balanced Class Weighting: Automatically adjusts loss weights W_j = N / (2 N_j) to resolve feedback class imbalances.
  • Explainable Feature Importance: Unpacks Gini-impurity drops across 9 dense feature dimensions.

4. Colorimetry & K-Means Fabric Clustering

  • K-Means Color Quantization: Clusters fabric pixels into dominant and secondary palette centroids.
  • HSV Color Wheel Trigonometry: Calculates hue separation angles (ΔH) to evaluate Complementary, Analogous, and Triadic harmonies.
  • CIE-Lab Euclidean Distance: Computes perceptual ΔE color differences matching human eye perception.

5. Streamlit Reactive Cloud Platform

  • Multi-Page Web Architecture: Decoupled UI pages with reactive session state caching.
  • Zero Server Cost Hosting: Optimized memory footprint allows continuous production hosting on Streamlit Cloud.
  • Mobile-First Responsive CSS: Tailored viewport styles optimized for smartphone camera uploads.

PROJECT CONCLUSION & FUTURE SCOPE

Conclusion: FitChecker demonstrates that an intelligent, zero-friction, production-grade digital wardrobe system can be built without relying on expensive third-party APIs. By combining classical computer vision (GrabCut with adaptive frame sampling) with explainable multi-objective mathematics, machine learning adaptation, and 24-shade personal colorimetry, FitChecker empowers users with personalized, confident daily styling.

Future Roadmap:

  • Client-Side WebAssembly (WASM): Running GrabCut on-device in browser threads to eliminate cloud compute bottlenecks.
  • Live Weather API Ingress: Fetching real-time temperature, rain, and humidity to adjust weather coefficients automatically.
  • 3D Parametric Body Fitting: Enabling 3D virtual try-ons to preview garment draping and proportion fit.
